plan: [I treat this as a common-value second-price auction. To avoid the winner’s curse, I bid my estimate of the common value conditional on my signal being the highest. With s=13 and three bidders, E[common | s=13 and I win] ≈ $22.9. I therefore place a bid of $22.9 (rounded to the $0.1 increment).]

[I compute the posterior for the common value given my signal 7: feasible common values are 20–27 (uniform), so E[C | signal=7] = 23.5. In a second-price auction with interdependent values, bidding the posterior expectation of the true value is the Bayes-Nash best response. I will bid $23.5 (allowed increment $0.1) to maximize expected profit while accounting for the winner’s curse.]
